subtitle: The Friday When Kashmir Held Its Breath

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of aged monarch over Srinagar
panels.action: Old Zain-ul-Abidin stands frail yet regal on a terrace above the Jhelum, Zaina Kadal bridge and the clustered roofs of Srinagar below, snow peaks distant, shadows of quarrelling sons implied in the background.

dialogue.text: On a Friday in May 1470, Budshah of Kashmir died fearing poison and surrounded by rival sons. Why did a golden age end in suspicion, and how did his valley mourn as his world unravelled?

i18n.hi: मई 1470 के एक जुमे को कश्मीर के बडशाह की मौत हुई, ज़हर के डर में, झगड़ालू बेटों से घिरा हुआ। सोने जैसा दौर शक में क्यों डूबा, और घाटी ने कैसे मातम किया जब उसका संसार बिखरने लगा?

panels.shot: slow push-in on weathered face
panels.action: Close on Zain-ul-Abidin’s lined face inside a dim palace room, his eyes sharp but ringed with fatigue as he looks past attendants toward the door, half in light, half in shadow.

dialogue.text: Srivara’s chronicle opens this chapter with an old king who had ruled for decades, now shrinking from court, suspicious of cups and counsel, listening for danger in every footstep.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा की दास्तान यहाँ खुलती है – बूढ़ा बादशाह, बरसों राज करके अब दरबार से कतराता, प्यासा शक में, सलाह से डरा हुआ, हर कदम में ख़तरे की आहट सुनता हुआ।

panels.shot: medium interior shot, chamber with food tray
panels.action: An attendant sets down a brass tray of food and a goblet before Zain-ul-Abidin; the Sultan, wrapped in shawls, hesitates, his hand hovering above the cup, gaze wary and tense.

dialogue.text: Late in his reign, Srivara says, fear of poisoning took hold. The Budshah who once sat open among scholars now ate and drank with caution, sensing plots even in daily bread.

i18n.hi: राज के आख़िरी वर्षों में, श्रीवरा लिखता है, ज़हर का डर दिल पर छा गया। जो बडशाह कभी विद्वानों के बीच खुला बैठता था, अब हर निवाले, हर घूँट में साज़िश सूँघकर संभलकर खाने लगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of deserted audience hall
panels.action: A grand audience hall stands largely empty, carved pillars receding into shadow; Zain-ul-Abidin sits alone on the throne, a few officials distant, scrolls piled unused beside him.

dialogue.text: He began to withdraw from daily government. Decisions passed more often through agents and ambitious sons. The hall that had seen land reforms and mercy now echoed with absence.

i18n.hi: वो रोज़मर्रा के राजकाज से हटने लगा। फ़ैसले अब कारिंदों और महत्वाकांक्षी बेटों के हाथ से ज़्यादा गुजरते। वही दीवान, जहाँ ज़मीन के सुधार और रहम देखे थे, अब ख़ालीपन की गूंज से भर गया।

panels.shot: animated map-style overhead of valley and routes
panels.action: Bird’s-eye of the Kashmir valley, Srinagar at its center, lines tracing toward outlying fortresses; small stylized banners mark separate forces, suggesting divided commands.

dialogue.text: Adam Khan, Haji Khan, Bahram Khan – powerful sons and kin – had once been instruments of expansion. Now, Majumdar notes, their rivalries strained the unity Budshah had built.

i18n.hi: आदम ख़ान, हाजी ख़ान, बहराम ख़ान – ताक़तवर बेटे और रिश्तेदार – कभी फ़तह के औज़ार थे। अब, मजुमदार लिखता है, उनकी टकराहटें बडशाह की गढ़ी एकता को चीरने लगीं।

panels.shot: intercut medium shots of three princely figures in tension
panels.action: Three princely silhouettes, each in a different setting—one in armor, one amid clerks, one in a riverside mansion—are shown in separate panels within the frame, each turned away from the others.

dialogue.text: Hasan recounts conflicts among Adam Khan, Haji Khan and Bahram Khan, as each sought advantage. The succession was unwritten, and ambition stepped into the gap.

i18n.hi: हसन लिखता है कि आदम ख़ान, हाजी ख़ान और बहराम ख़ान में भिड़ंतें बढ़ीं, हर कोई बढ़त चाहता था। उतराधिकार लिखा न था, और उसी खाली जगह में लालच कदम रख गया।

panels.shot: low-angle interior, throne room with distant argument
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin sits slightly turned on his throne, listening as two unseen male voices argue beyond a half-open doorway, his fingers tightening on the armrest, attendants frozen.

dialogue.text: From his seat he could hear raised voices and clashing claims. The Budshah who had once stilled factions between Hindus and Muslims now faced unrest within his own house.

i18n.hi: अपने तख़्त से ही उसे ऊँची आवाज़ें, टकराती दावेदारियाँ सुनाई देतीं। जो बडशाह कभी हिंदू–मुसलमान के झगड़े थाम देता था, अब अपने ही घर के तूफ़ान से जूझ रहा था।

panels.shot: intimate interior close-up with physician
panels.action: An elderly court physician gently lifts Zain-ul-Abidin’s wrist to feel his pulse; the Sultan’s gaze drifts toward a latticed window, where late spring light filters in.

dialogue.speaker: zain_ul_abidin
dialogue.text: My reign is long. My time is short.

i18n.hi: मेरा राज लंबा है। मेरी मोहलत छोटी।

panels.shot: soft wide shot of prayer space
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin, wrapped in white, sits on a prayer mat facing a niche, hands slightly raised, the chamber plain, a brazier burning low, an attendant respectfully distant.

dialogue.text: Srivara places his final illness in the spring of 1470. The Sultan turned more to prayer and solitude, as the machinery of rule creaked on without his full hand upon it.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा उसका अंतिम रोग 1470 की बहार में रखता है। सुल्तान इबादत और तन्हाई में डूबता गया, जबकि राज की मशीनरी बिना उसकी पूरी पकड़ के चरमराती चलती रही।

panels.shot: medium shot, dawn light, bedchamber
panels.action: On a simple bed within a royal chamber, Zain-ul-Abidin lies propped on cushions, frail but composed; through the window, dawn over Srinagar hints at Friday prayers in the city.

dialogue.text: On Friday, 12 May 1470, Srivara records, Budshah’s last day came. Outside, the valley woke to the call of prayer; inside, the man who had shaped it lay near the end.

i18n.hi: जुमे, 12 मई 1470 को, श्रीवरा लिखता है, बडशाह का आख़िरी दिन आया। बाहर घाटी अज़ान से जागी; अंदर, जिसने इसे गढ़ा था, वो ज़िंदगी के किनारे लेटा था।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on eyes closing
panels.action: Extreme close-up of Zain-ul-Abidin’s face as his eyes gently close, lines of age relaxed, a faint hint of a breath leaving, the background fading into soft blur.

dialogue.text: After a reign remembered for peace and building, the chronicler says, he died on that Friday. No battle cry, no court drama at the bedside—only an old king’s quiet departure.

i18n.hi: अमन और तामीरात के लिए याद किए जाने वाले राज के बाद, तारीख़नवीस कहता है, वो उसी जुमे को चला गया। न जंग का नारा, न बिस्तर के पास दरबारी तमाशा—सिर्फ़ एक बूढ़े बादशाह की चुप रवाना।

panels.shot: wide shot of Zaina Kadal over Jhelum
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Zaina Kadal bridge spanning the Jhelum, crowded with people moving somberly toward the far bank, wooden houses leaning over the water, mountains hazy beyond.

dialogue.text: Word spread fast along the Jhelum. At Zaina Kadal, the bridge he had built, crowds pressed together, crossing toward Mazar-e-Salatin, each step heavy with news of Budshah’s death.

i18n.hi: ख़बर झेलम के किनारे-किनारे दौड़ गई। ज़ैना कदल, उस पुल पर जो उसने बनवाया था, हुजूम ठसाठस भर गया, मज़ार-ए-सलातिन की तरफ़ पुल पार करते कदम, बडशाह की मौत की ख़बर से भारी।

panels.shot: high-angle shot over Mazar-e-Salatin grounds
panels.action: Bird’s-eye of Mazar-e-Salatin near Zaina Kadal, an open burial ground beside the river, thronged by men and women in plain clothes, many sitting or standing in silence.

dialogue.text: Srivara describes his funeral at Mazar-e-Salatin, the cemetery of kings. From town and countryside they came, filling the banks and fields, the valley briefly gathered in one place.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा उसका जनाज़ा मज़ार-ए-सलातिन, बादशाहों के कब्रिस्तान में बयान करता है। शहर और देहात से लोग उमड़ पड़े, घाट के किनारे और खेत भर दिए, जैसे पूरी घाटी एक जगह जमा हो गई हो।

panels.shot: medium crowd shot focusing on fasting mourners
panels.action: A group of mourners, some with rosaries, others with hands clasped, sit together on the ground, bowls untouched beside them, faces drawn in grief as they observe a fast.

dialogue.text: The chronicler notes fasting and lamentation. People abstained from food, recited verses, and wept for the ruler who had repaired temples, patronised learning, and eased taxes.

i18n.hi: तारीख़नवीस रोज़े और मातम का ज़िक्र करता है। लोग खाने से रुके, आयतें पढ़ीं, और उस हाकिम के लिए रोए जिसने मंदिर सुधारे, इल्म को सहारा दिया, और लगान हल्की की।

panels.shot: low-angle of the grave being covered
panels.action: Hands of attendants and labourers gently lower a cloth-covered bier into a prepared grave at Mazar-e-Salatin, then begin to pour earth with care, a simple stone nearby.

dialogue.text: In that soil near the bridge, they laid him among other sultans. Lawrence later walked these grounds, noting how memory of Budshah lingered in the landscape itself.

i18n.hi: पुल के पास की उसी मिट्टी में, उन्हें उसे बाकी सुल्तानों के बीच सुलाना पड़ा। बाद में लॉरेंस इन ज़मीनों पर चला, नोट करता कि बडशाह की याद खुद नज़ारे में बसी रहती है।

panels.shot: split-frame showing throne and grave
panels.action: The frame is divided: on one side, an empty throne in the palace; on the other, the fresh grave at Mazar-e-Salatin, mourners departing, the river flowing steadily between worlds.

dialogue.text: Even as his grave settled, the throne stood empty. The valley had shown unity in grief, but the question of who could hold his settlement together hung unanswered.

i18n.hi: उसकी क़ब्र बैठ रही थी, पर तख़्त खाली खड़ा था। घाटी दुख में तो एक हुई, पर ये सवाल कि उसकी बसाई सुलह किसके हाथ टिकेगी, हवा में लटका रह गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a new, younger Sultan on throne
panels.action: A younger Sultan—Haidar Shah—sits on the same throne, flanked by courtiers; his posture unsure, the hall less crowded, banners drooping slightly compared to earlier splendor.

dialogue.text: Haidar Shah succeeded him, then Hasan Shah. Historians describe their rule as weaker, unable to match Budshah’s balance of firmness and concession that had kept factions in check.

i18n.hi: उसके बाद हैदर शाह आया, फिर हसन शाह। इतिहासकार उनके राज को कमज़ोर बताते हैं, बडशाह की उस सख़्ती और नरमी के संतुलन से दूर जो फिरेकों को काबू में रखता था।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of Srinagar changing banners
panels.action: A stylised wide view of Srinagar over time: palace banners change, soldiers’ dress shifts, small groups of Chak warriors appear in a later layer, hinting at new power centers.

dialogue.text: As Shah Mir successors weakened, Chak chiefs rose. Over the next century, power shifted again and again in the valley Budshah had once steadied, its politics growing harsher.

i18n.hi: शाह मीर के उत्तराधिकारी ढीले पड़े तो चाक सरदार उठने लगे। अगले सौ साल में वही घाटी, जिसे बडशाह ने थामा था, बार-बार हाथ बदलती रही, सियासत और तल्ख़ होती गई।

panels.shot: expansive map-view showing Kashmir and Mughal domains
panels.action: A map-style view shows Kashmir in the mountains, then faint overlaid outlines of the expanding Mughal domains reaching northward by 1586, Kashmir drawn within their frontier.

dialogue.text: By 1586, the Mughals annexed Kashmir. Between Budshah’s peaceful Friday death and that conquest lay a chain of succession strains and shifting alliances that his late fears had foreshadowed.

i18n.hi: 1586 तक आते-आते, मुग़ल ने कश्मीर का इलहाक कर लिया। बडशाह की उस पुरअमन जुमे की मौत से लेकर इस फ़तह तक उतराधिकार की खिंचतान और बदलती यारियाँ की लड़ी चली, जिनकी परछाईं उसके आख़िरी डर में दिख चुकी थी।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide of grave and bridge at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, Zaina Kadal and the Jhelum lie quiet; in the foreground, Budshah’s grave stone at Mazar-e-Salatin is seen from behind, as if we stand where he rests, watching the city he shaped.

dialogue.text: Budshah’s Friday reminds us that even a just and able reign cannot outlive an unsettled succession; memory may honour a ruler, but only stable heirs can guard what he built after he is gone.

i18n.hi: बडशाह का जुमे वाला दिन याद दिलाता है कि नेक और काबिल राज भी उलझे उत्तराधिकार से आगे नहीं जी सकता; यादें बादशाह को सलाम करती हैं, पर सिर्फ़ मज़बूत वारिस उसकी बनाई चीज़ों की रखवाली कर सकते हैं जब वो नहीं रहता।
